sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.

sentences.text: It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel has further stated that the victim is the consenting party, as is evident from her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. and she has expressed her willingness to live with the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The victim was pregnant at the time of her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: Subsequent to it, she has given birth to a baby boy.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant is ready to take care of the offspring, who has taken birth out of the said corporeal relationship with the victim.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

sentences.text: In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

sentences.text: 8. Learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application but has not disputed the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant and the aforesaid submissions of learned counsel for the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text:
9. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs.
Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785 this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text:
Niranjan Singh and another vs.
Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: 10. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: 11. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text:
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
12.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: 13. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text:

sentences._hearing_file: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 March, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

sentences.text: No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

sentences.text: 16. Let the applicant- Sunny involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall deposit an amount of Rs. 3 lakhs to the account of the child of the victim within a period of one month of his release.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

sentences.text: 17. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
